# Child Activation Functions

A function library for preparing child documents with declared parties, transport channels and references to timeline-access evidence. It supports explicit mappings between independently named child and parent roles, plus legacy construction using the parent's role names.

The child-building functions read the executing document and return a modified `child`. They do not initialize that child, record participant acceptance or grant timeline access. The library also inherits activation, party-mapping, access and amendment helpers; installing a caller determines when those helpers execute.

## Explicit child preparation

`prepareChild(child, mapping, suppliedRoles)` requires an uninitialized child with the exact `Activation Clause` at `/clauses/activation/type`. An existing `/contracts/initialized` causes `CHILD_ALREADY_INITIALIZED`; a different activation type causes `CHILD_ACTIVATION_REQUIRED`. `bindChild(child, mapping)` calls it with an empty `suppliedRoles` list.

Child declarations come from `/clauses/activation/parameters/parties`; source parties come from the executing document's `/activation/parties`. Both must be nonempty objects, and `mapping` must be an object keyed by declared child roles. Each mapping value is either a source-role name or an explicit `Party`. Selected parties must have a `lead/channel` and a nonempty, duplicate-free list of nonempty text `readerKeys`. The resolver checks `Party` compatibility and constructs a specialization using the child declaration.

Every child role needs a mapping unless listed in `suppliedRoles`. Such a supplied role must be declared and unmapped; its declaration is retained. Every source party must remain represented in the resulting roster by the same exact lead channel and the same primary reader-key set, regardless of key order. A representative or descriptive business identity does not substitute for that main identity. Child role names must be nonempty and contain none of `.`, `/`, `~` or `__`.

Preparation replaces the child's party declarations with the resolved roster while preserving its other activation parameters. It preserves existing child `accessPaths`, defaulting a missing list to `[]`, and appends references to the executing document's activation access documents. New references occupy `/timelineAccess/configurerN`, where numbering starts from the existing path count. An occupied target fails with `CHILD_ACCESS_PATH_CONFLICT`.

For roster entries with a `lead/channel`, transports are installed under `/contracts`: the lead uses the child role name, and additional representatives use `role__representativeId`. An identical existing channel is accepted; a different one causes `CHILD_CHANNEL_CONFLICT`. Retaining a supplied declaration without a lead channel does not establish that the party is resolved or ready for initialization.

## Legacy construction

`activateChild(child, frozen, roles, readerNames)` returns `child` unchanged when the executing document has no `/activation`. Otherwise, an empty `roles` list selects every parent party; `readerNames` selects only the explicitly named additional reader groups. Unknown names cause `CHILD_PARTY_NOT_IN_PARENT` or `CHILD_READER_NOT_IN_PARENT`.

It rebuilds the child's `timelineAccess` map using `grantN` references and replaces its activation clause. Existing activation parameters are retained except that `parties`, `readers`, `accessPaths` and the Boolean `frozen` are supplied by this call. Existing `required` is preserved, or explicitly set to `[]` when absent. This differs from ordinary Activation Clause initialization, where omitted `required` defaults to all roster roles. The legacy function writes selected transports without the initialization and collision guards used by `prepareChild`.

On later Activation Clause initialization, `revision` defaults to `1`, `allowNewParties` to `false`, and `readers` and `accessPaths` to empty collections when omitted. Roster freezing follows `frozen` or a true `/partyRosterFrozen`. Preparation alone does not run this initialization.

## Inherited activation and access behavior

Inherited state belongs to the document where these helpers execute. A returned child's eventual `/activation` belongs to that child, not to its parent.

- `approve` requires exact-document review, a current party-lead channel, the current activation `revision` and sufficient participant access. Negotiation-enabled configurations also require `termsRef`; any supplied reference must match current terms. A new approval records the party's flag, commits activation state and emits `Terms Accepted`. Repeating an existing approval still passes the guards but records no new acceptance event. `approveWithTerms` delegates to the same checks.
- `computeState` distinguishes access readiness, acceptance and closure. Acceptance requires every `required` role's approval and unchanged agreed term fields. `ACTIVE` requires acceptance, access and an open document. Other statuses are `WAITING_FOR_ACCESS` before first activation, `SUSPENDED_ACCESS` after prior activation when access is missing, `AWAITING_ACCEPTANCE` when access exists but acceptance is incomplete, and `CLOSED` when closed. Access evaluation also includes pending party additions whose expected revision is current. `commitState` retains `everActivated` and emits first-activation, access-suspension and access-restoration events at the corresponding transitions.
- Access checks treat transports matching `External Channel` as requiring no access-document match. Other transports must be `Timeline Channel`. For each such transport, one referenced `Timeline Access` document must match its timeline and provider and contain at least one alternative key from every reader group, including party, representative and additional named groups. Merely copying a reference does not satisfy these checks.
- `updateParty` requires exact-document review, an unfrozen roster and a party lead. A lead may replace its own party; adding another named party also requires `allowNewParties`. Replacement data needs a lead channel, valid representative names and adequate access. Successful changes check contract-name conflicts, clear approvals, increment `revision`, add a new party to `required` when applicable, and emit `Party Changed`.
- `admitApprovedParties` requires an unfrozen roster, matching `expectedRevision`, a configured admission-approver list and sufficient access. Existing roles must retain their main identity; new roles are added without automatically joining `required`. An unchanged roster returns `duplicate`. `requestPartyAddition` ignores stale or already recorded requests, checks supplied access documents and records missing-access requests. `Party Access Update Requested` expresses a request, not permission or participant consent.
- `installTimelineAccess` accepts 1–16 documents, validates their initialized native access policy and recorded provider history, deduplicates them by original document identity, and registers update channels using the existing activation-refresh steps. It embeds evidence; it does not change provider permission sets.

`initializeTerms` establishes a terms reference and `termsRevision`, initially `1`, with negotiation initially editable. Negotiable fields must exist and be scalar. The terms definition excludes referenced access documents, activation `accessPaths` and `readers`, and party-level `readerKeys`. Roster or required-role changes revise the terms identity, close a pending proposal as `AUTHORITY_CHANGED`, and clear approvals when negotiation is enabled. Successful activation through `approve` freezes negotiation and closes any remaining proposal as `SUPERSEDED`.

Inherited amendment helpers receive `bindings.state`, `bindings.editable`, `parameters.paths` and `parameters.approvers` as caller arguments. Recording checks revision, allowed path, editability and proposal identity; approval requires a configured approver. The replacement is applied only after all configured approvers have approved. Duplicate records or approvals do not apply another change; conflicting, reused, stale or frozen proposals are rejected.

`requireActive` checks recorded activation and current access, and additionally checks current party or representative membership when `workflow` is true. With no `/activation`, both `requireActive` and `businessReady` permit pass-through; that fallback is not evidence that activation occurred.
